A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAISI research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture, Lorenz ’63, SQG, and SEVIR experiments, including numerical metrics, filtering visualizations, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SDA comparisons, additional SEVIR baselines, and moving-observation experiments.

M1.justification: DAISI’s forecast, inverse-SDE, and guided-sampling procedure remains unchanged. However, v2 proposes an auxiliary sliding-window filtering adaptation of SDA, with state propagation and final-window-state retention specified in Appendix D.4.3 and Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: The underlying toy problem, L63, SQG, and SEVIR coverage is retained. v2 adds moving-band SQG observations and replaces high-resolution point sensing with coarse, locally averaged observations. It also adds SDA smoothing evaluations alongside filtering on retained datasets.

E2.justification: v2 adds SDA filtering and smoothing comparisons across the four main SQG-64 settings and SEVIR, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set. LETKF and EnSF also gain SEVIR results where v1 reported only DAISI and FlowDAS. The corrected expansion of LETKF’s name does not represent a different baseline.

E3.justification: The High-dim. experiment changes from direct observations with noise SD 3 to subsampling at 64×64, averaging 5×5 neighborhoods, and observing 5% of those pixels with SD 1. DAISI’s tmin changes from 0.4 to 0.0 (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 10). Added SDA evaluations introduce full-trajectory smoothing versus five-state sliding-window filtering, with separately specified guidance and solver settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a robustness check using a four-pixel observation band moving four pixels each step, with metric trajectories and uncertainty visualizations in Figures 13–14. The existing inversion, SDEdit, forecast-model, hyperparameter, and assimilation-interval ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across ten experiments or trajectories for the summarized comparisons and show L63 99% credible intervals. v2 applies the same reporting practice to added baselines. Changed SSR means and deviations are result changes, not new uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline results: for example, Noisy CRPS is 1.13±0.10 for SDA filtering versus DAISI’s retained 1.32±0.13 (Table 12). SEVIR gains LETKF and EnSF results, while DAISI’s SEVIR SSR changes from 1.142±0.10 to 1.19±0.12 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 13). Moving-observation results are new, and high-resolution curves and samples are replaced under changed conditions, precluding a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the conditional density in the score derivation from p(zt|z1) to p(z1|zt) (v1 Equation 38; v2 Equation 39), and replaces an erroneous equality with an inequality in the entropy proof (v1 Equation 117; v2 Equation 118). Section 3.2 also drops the horizon factor N from the stated complexity expressions. The main entropy bound and assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: a stationary generative prior combined with forecast inversion, no retraining at each assimilation step, compatibility with numerical and learned forecasts, and expressive inference under challenging observations. The revised abstract and shortened conclusion preserve this substantive scope.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the forecast-support explanation for FlowDAS failures with a local-conditional versus filtering-distribution mismatch. It adds qualifications about SDA’s smoothing advantage and high-resolution artifacts, and narrows tracking 'all' plausible modes to 'many.' It removes the generative-prior spectral-bias discussion and debiasing/adaptive-noise future directions. DAISI’s inexact-filtering caveat remains in Section 3.1.

D1.justification: v2 adds SDA implementation and training details, including the U-Net source, five-state window, 4096 epochs, AdamW settings, and guidance/solver configurations in Tables 6–7. It also documents moving-observation construction and additional LETKF/DAISI settings. The existing DAISI architecture and training documentation are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds works by Chung et al. (2025), Zhao et al. (2025), Tian et al. (2024), and Shysheya et al. (2024). It refines positioning against FlowDAS and GenCast through conditional-target mismatch and particle-weight degeneracy, while retaining the broader hybrid-EnVar and diffusion-assimilation positioning.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and introduction, simplifies deterministic-flow notation, corrects terminology, and adds Section 4.4. It merges and substantially shortens the conclusion and limitations into 'Conclusion and Outlook.' These are localized revisions within a largely retained document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 2, SDA configuration tables, and two moving-observation figures. It substantially expands the appendix comparison tables and image panels, adds SDA curves with revised legends and axes, and redraws high-resolution outputs. Existing ablation displays are largely retained and relocated rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The SDA comparisons and added LETKF/EnSF SEVIR results make the empirical positioning better supported, including cases where competitors outperform or closely match DAISI. Explicitly separating smoothing from filtering, correcting derivations, and testing moving observations further improve the assessment. These benefits outweigh the reduced limitations discussion, although losing the prior spectral-bias and debiasing discussion limits the net gain.
